turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, we'll do the obs first. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven.
[SEG0002] person_1 (NURSE): Temp is thirty-eight point three. Pulse, uh, I nearly charted eighty-eight. No, it's ninety-four.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Weight today is twenty-four kilograms. Last time in March you were sixty-eight, that was the heart rate, and your last pressure was one-forty. Old numbers, not today's.
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ta. Sorry, drop-off was a mess and then we couldn't find a park.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): All good. Grab a seat. What are we sorting?
[SEG0006] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His eyes. School wants a note or they won't have him back. They've been red and sticky after a cold.
[SEG0007] person_4 (PATIENT): It's nothing. I'm fine.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Which eye, and how long has it been?

[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Left one started about three days ago. Err, actually I can't pin the morning, might've been Friday night or Saturday. Then the right one went red yesterday. Both of them now, sticky gunky lashes in the morning.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the eye painful? The eyeball itself, not just the crust.
[SEG0011] person_4 (PATIENT): No. Doesn't hurt.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Itchy at all?
[SEG0013] person_4 (PATIENT): Nuh. It's fine.

[SEG0014] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He had a cold all last week. Runny nose, a cough. That's mostly gone now. I've been giving children's panadol, five mils, that's two hundred and forty milligrams, by mouth, morning and night since yesterday, for the temperature.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Is the discharge just mornings, or through the day?
[SEG0016] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mostly mornings. Yellow, a bit green. He rubs it and it looks angrier.
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): Well actually it is itchy. When I rub it. Heaps.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. So the itch is there. Are the lids swollen? Is the light bothering him?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Puffy lids in the morning, then it settles a bit. Light's fine, he's not squinting.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Can you see the board at school?
[SEG0021] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah. I can see. Not a big deal.
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He says that about everything. The teacher reckons it's conjunctivitis and wants him off. He just wants his footy.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Both conjunctivae are red, left more than right. Some crust on the lashes.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): The cornea is clear. No real lid swelling just now. Pupils are equal.

[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm turning it over in my head. After a cold, both eyes sticky and red, with a bit of fever, my leaning is a viral conjunctivitis. I can't fully rule out an early bacterial one, but I'm not going to conclude that today, and allergy doesn't really fit the gunk.
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The chemist mentioned cloramphenicol drops. Should we grab some?
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. I wouldn't start an antibiotic. That sort of drop won't change the usual viral course, and there's no reason for it today.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cooled boiled water, a clean cotton pad, one pad for each eye, wipe from inside to out. Wash his hands, his own towel, no sharing pillows. Bin the pads straight after.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): School-wise, not tomorrow. Once the discharge has dried up, usually a couple of days, he can go back. I'll write the note they want.
[SEG0030] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's been tired, and a bit off his food, since the cold. He's drinking, just not loads.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any tummy pain, vomiting, or diarrhoea? Any earache?
[SEG0032] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No tummy pain. No vomiting. No diarrhoea. Ears are fine.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Breathing been alright? Any chest symptoms at all?
[SEG0034] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Breathing's fine. No chest stuff.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Panadol can continue if he's miserable. Same two hundred and forty milligrams, up to four times a day, at least four hours apart. Don't add nurofen on top unless we've talked about it.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Often three to five days. If it's not settling in three days, or the eye becomes painful, the light really hurts, or his vision drops, come straight back. Sooner if he seems properly worse.
[SEG0037] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the note for school?

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yep, I'll do it before you leave. Viral-type conjunctivitis, keep him home till the sticky discharge settles, likely back in a couple of days. Reception will print you a copy.
[SEG0039] person_4 (PATIENT): So Saturday footy?
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the eyes aren't gunky by then, yes. If they're still stuck shut, you sit it out.
[SEG0041] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Beauty. Thanks for that.

spec.situation: Parent with a child with red sticky eye after a cold; school wants a note; one eye then both; no eye pain; doctor advises hygiene, no antibiotic, explains return advice.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
